SCHILLER official on Instagram‎: "Happy Nowruz 💚🤍❤️

Dear friends in Iran and around the world—this year feels different. It’s hard, heavy, and uncertain. For many of you, this isn’t just another new year… it comes in the middle of fear, loss, and constant pressure. And honestly, words from afar don’t change that.

Thinking of you alone doesn’t fix anything. It doesn’t make things safer. It doesn’t make life easier. But still—I want you to know you are not forgotten.

I think of you often. Not in a distant, symbolic way, but with real concern for your daily lives, your families, your future. I see your resilience, even when you’re tired. I see how much you carry, even when the world moves on.

And more than anything, I am reminded that freedom is not something abstract—it is the most important thing in life. The ability to live without fear, to speak, to choose, to simply exist with dignity… this is what every human being deserves 🤍

Nowruz is about a “new day” — about renewal, even after darkness. And maybe this year, that idea feels far away. Hope doesn’t always feel strong or beautiful. Sometimes it’s just quiet endurance.

For the new year, I don’t wish you empty words. I wish you safety. I wish you moments of relief. I wish you strength when things feel overwhelming, and small pockets of peace where you can breathe 🌱

And even if it takes time—more time than any of us want—light will prevail. Not magically, not easily, but because people like you keep going 🕊️✨

Happy Nowruz 🤍

- - - - - - 

Nowruz (Persian: نوروز, Iranian Persian: [noːˈɾuːz],[w] lit. 'New Day') is the Iranian or Persian New Year's day. Historically, it has been observed by Iranian peoples, but is now celebrated by many ethnicities worldwide. It is a festival based on the Northern Hemisphere spring equinox, which marks the first day of a new year on the Iranian calendars and the currently used Solar Hijri calendar; it usually coincides with a date between 19 March and 22 March on the Gregorian calendar.
